questions.question: Which language should the web app use?
questions.rationale: TypeScript is a strong default for a maintainable full-stack application.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed JavaScript for safer application development.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Standard JavaScript without static types.

questions.question: Would you like to use Next.js for the web app, or prefer a React single-page app?
questions.rationale: Next.js supports the existing React-style interface and can host the application API in one deployable project.

options.label: Next.js
options.description: React framework with routing and server-side API capabilities; recommended for a unified web app and backend.

options.label: React single-page app
options.description: React frontend separated from a dedicated backend API.

questions.question: Keep the existing appearance and flows; replace demo/local-only profile, class, booking, coach-dashboard, and verification behavior with production-ready frontend interactions connected to the backend.
questions.answer: Preserve current UI and features; wire them to the live backend.
questions.rationale: The request is an upgrade of the current frontend, not a redesign.
questions.recommendedChoice: Preserve current UI and features; wire them to the live backend.

questions.question: Which language should the backend use?
questions.rationale: TypeScript allows the web app and API to share types and fits the requested Next.js/React ecosystem.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed JavaScript suitable for the application API.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Standard JavaScript without static types.

questions.question: Which framework should implement the application API? If you choose a custom framework, specify it.
questions.rationale: Route Handlers keep the backend alongside the frontend when Next.js is selected; if React SPA is preferred, a separate Node.js API framework can be selected in the response.

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Managed serverless API functions; requires an Azure storage account for runtime storage.

questions.question: Implement secure APIs for member profiles, classes, bookings, coach dashboard operations, and time-limited SMS verification codes. Store provider configuration and database credentials only in environment variables; do not enter secrets in this form.
questions.answer: Profiles, classes, bookings, coach operations, and SMS OTP verification backed by MongoDB.
questions.rationale: These are the existing application flows and the requested production upgrade.
questions.recommendedChoice: Profiles, classes, bookings, coach operations, and SMS OTP verification backed by MongoDB.

questions.question: Which data stores does the application need?
questions.rationale: The user has selected MongoDB. A separate blob store is not inferred because no file or media storage requirement was specified.

options.label: MongoDB
options.description: Use the existing MongoDB database for profiles, classes, bookings, and related application records.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: The application does not persist data in a database or storage service.

questions.question: Will users sign in to use application features?
questions.rationale: Member profiles and bookings require identifying users; profile creation is explicitly being updated to use verification codes.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users authenticate to access their profiles and application features.

options.label: No
options.description: Application features are available without user sign-in.

questions.question: Which SMS provider should send profile verification codes? Do not enter credentials here; configure any account keys through environment variables.
questions.rationale: The current app only demonstrates OTP output in the console; a real provider and its environment configuration are needed for delivery.

options.label: Twilio
options.description: Use a Twilio SMS account; configure account credentials and sender details through environment variables.

options.label: Azure Communication Services
options.description: Use Azure Communication Services SMS; configure the connection and sender settings outside source control.

options.label: Another provider
options.description: Specify the existing or preferred SMS provider in the form.

options.label: I need help choosing
options.description: Plan a provider-agnostic SMS integration and confirm the provider before enabling real delivery.

questions.question: How will the existing MongoDB connection be configured? Do not paste a connection string or credentials here.
questions.answer: Use an environment variable; I will configure it locally/deployed
questions.rationale: The connection must be provided securely outside the application source.

options.label: Use an environment variable; I will configure it locally/deployed
options.description: The application will read the MongoDB URI from a documented environment variable such as MONGODB_URI.

options.label: I need setup guidance
options.description: Include instructions for securely supplying the existing MongoDB URI in local and deployed environments.

questions.recommendedChoice: Use an environment variable; I will configure it locally/deployed

questions.question: Do you have a preferred deployment target, or should the plan focus on local development first and keep hosting portable?
questions.answer: Local development first; keep hosting portable
questions.rationale: No cloud host was requested. A portable plan avoids assuming Azure or another provider.

options.label: Local development first; keep hosting portable
options.description: Implement and verify locally, with hosting decisions deferred.

options.label: Azure
options.description: Plan deployment to an appropriate Azure host.

options.label: Vercel
options.description: Plan deployment to Vercel.

options.label: Another target
options.description: Specify a different preferred hosting provider.
